counterfactual_missing_items: No mucosal erosions are explicitly described
No culprit drug or infectious trigger is stated
The photo-induced ACLE history and anti-dsDNA/hypocomplementemia could alternatively suggest active lupus
decisive_items: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
Acute stratum corneum present overlying full thickness epithelial necrosis
response.rationale: R5 is supported by the full cluster of raw findings: widespread atypical/dusky target lesions, tender blistering, and full-thickness epidermal necrosis, together diagnostic of SJS. R1 only accounts for the antecedent photo-induced ACLE and malar rash; R2 only supports background SLE; R4 and R3 cite nonspecific labs; C1 redundantly appends the atypical-target descriptor to R5 without independent raw evidence.

rejected.why: Redundant completion of R5; no independent raw span, just the same atypical-target text already subsumed by R5.
Anemia and hypocomplementemia are nonspecific and do not establish nephritis; no renal-specific raw evidence.
Thrombocytopenia is an isolated lab finding, not the cause of the presenting eruption.
SLE history and serologies confirm background disease but do not explain the acute targetoid blistering and epidermal necrosis.
